record.field: Immich: your photo library in Odoo

Your organization keeps its photos in Immich, the self-hosted photo library. This short course shows how to reach those photos from inside Odoo, so you stop re-uploading the same pictures into every document you write.

Work through the four lessons in order. The first one connects Odoo to your Immich server; the rest assume that connection exists.
1. Connect Odoo to your Immich server

What you need

Two things belong together — a URL and an API key:

  • Server URL — where your Immich server answers, e.g. https://photos.example.com. No trailing slash is needed; Odoo strips it.
  • API key — a personal key from your own Immich account.

Get the API key from Immich

  1. Open your Immich server and log in.
  2. Click your avatar, top right, and choose Account Settings.
  3. Open API Keys, then New API Key.
  4. Give it a name you will recognize — for example "Odoo" — and create it.
  5. Copy the key now. Immich shows it only once.

Treat the key like a password. It grants access to your photos for as long as it exists. If it leaks, delete it in Immich and create a new one.

Enter both values in Odoo

  1. Go to Settings ▸ General Settings.
  2. Find the block Immich Image Library.
  3. Paste the server URL and the API key.
  4. Save.

If it does not work

  • Nothing appears when you search — the key was probably pasted with surrounding whitespace, or it belongs to a different server than the URL says.
  • Permission denied — only administrators and website editors can change these settings. Ask one of them, or ask to be added to the website editor group.
  • The server is unreachable — Odoo runs on the server side. If Odoo cannot reach your Immich URL (firewall, internal hostname), no amount of correct credentials helps. Test the URL from a browser on the Odoo host.

Three ways to search

The Immich search bar sits in the image library dialog, next to the normal Odoo search. It understands more than filenames:

  • Content — describe what is in the picture: "red barn in snow", "invoice on a desk". This uses Immich's machine learning service.
  • People — type a name that Immich has recognized and you get that person's photos.
  • Metadata — filename, description and location are matched too, so an old, well-named archive is still searchable.

Why content search sometimes fails

Content search depends on immich-machine-learning running on the Immich server. If it is down, or still indexing, content search returns nothing while people and metadata search keep working. That asymmetry is the tell: if only content search is empty, the problem is on the Immich side, not in Odoo.

Practical habits

  • Search with a few concrete nouns rather than a sentence — "harbour crane sunset" beats "a picture of a crane at the harbour at sunset".
  • Only still images are offered. Videos in Immich are filtered out, because Odoo content needs an image.
  • If a person is missing, Immich has not grouped those faces yet. Name them in Immich first.
3. Put a photo into your content

Where the search bar appears

Everywhere Odoo opens its image library: the website editor, knowledge articles, the document app, product images and email templates. If you can insert an image, you can reach Immich.

Insert a photo

  1. Open the image library from the editor (Insert ▸ Image).
  2. Switch to the Immich tab.
  3. Search, then click the photo you want.
  4. Confirm. The image is now part of the Odoo record.

What actually happens to the file

The photo is copied into Odoo as an attachment. The original stays in Immich. That is deliberate: Immich remains the source of truth, and Odoo keeps a fixed copy so the page does not break if the Immich asset is later deleted or the server is unreachable.

Two consequences worth knowing:

  • Editing the photo in Immich later does not update the copy already in Odoo. Re-insert it if the change matters.
  • Deleting the Odoo record removes Odoo's copy only — never the Immich original. Immich deletes are done in Immich.

Mind the resolution

What you insert is the full-resolution original. A 50-megapixel photo makes a heavy web page. For website pages, prefer photos that are already sensibly sized, or let Odoo's image resizing handle the display size.
4. Who can see what — sharing and limits

The key decides, not the Odoo user

This is the one thing to get right. Odoo talks to Immich with one shared API key, configured once in the settings. That key carries the permissions of the Immich account that created it.

So: an Odoo user who can open the image library sees whatever the key can see. Odoo does not ask Immich "who is this user?" on every search.

What follows from that

  • If the key belongs to an Immich administrator, every Odoo user who can insert images can reach every photo that administrator can reach — including other people's libraries, if that Immich is shared.
  • If the key belongs to an ordinary Immich user, the search is limited to what that user is allowed to see.
  • Revoking access is done in Immich: delete the API key. Odoo then simply stops finding photos, until a new key is entered.

Choosing the right account

Create a dedicated Immich account for the Odoo integration rather than using a personal one. Give it access to a shared or company library, not to private photo collections. Then the key can be rotated — or the account disabled — without anyone losing their own photos or password.

Before you invite people

  • Decide which Immich library the Odoo key should reach. Configure that first, then invite users.
  • Remember that the integration cannot tell Odoo users apart. If different teams must not see each other's photos, that separation has to exist in Immich itself, or each team needs its own Odoo instance.
  • Only administrators and website editors can change the connection. Everyone else uses it.

You are done

Connect, search, insert, and understand the reach of the key. That is the whole integration. If something behaves oddly, the first question is always: what can the API key see?
